selectivity.text: Positive control for the JAK class, not a proposal for a JAK2-selective drug. Among the JAK kinases the human genetic support sits on JAK2 (genetic_association = 0.8458), yet the JAK inhibitors that worked in UC trials are tofacitinib, which like the others inhibits JAK1-dependent pathways most potently, and the selective JAK2 inhibitor upadacitinib and JAK1-preferential filgotinib; the TYK2-selective deucravacitinib did not show significant benefit in UC phase 2, whereas the TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor brepocitinib did. JAK2 also carries erythropoietin and thrombopoietin receptor signals, so selective JAK2 blockade would act on blood cell production. Its expression rises only modestly (log2fc = 0.833).

subunit.text: Human genetics separates causes from consequences. IL12B carries a strong Open Targets genetic association with UC (genetic_association = 0.8864) and is the strongest plasma Mendelian randomisation result among this atlas's genes: genetically higher protein raises UC risk (odds_ratio_per_sd = 1.539), so inhibition is the protective direction. IL12B is the p19 subunit of interleukin-12 and interleukin-23: ustekinumab binds it and was more effective than placebo in UC, and the anti-p19 antibodies mirikizumab, risankizumab and guselkumab, which bind IL23A and block interleukin-23 only, were effective too, which shows that blocking interleukin-23 alone is enough; whether blocking interleukin-12 adds benefit is not settled by these trials. For CD274 (PD-L1) genetics points the other way: higher plasma protein lowers UC risk (odds_ratio_per_sd = 0.595).

stage.text: Made mostly by neutrophils and myeloid cells (neutrophil_share_inflamed = 0.894), higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa and associated with ustekinumab non-response and placebo non-response alike; nangibotide is approved for UC.

overclaimed novelty.text: Validated target: the largest pooled increase of the first-in-class candidates, up in (cohorts_up = 7) cohorts, made by stromal cells (mostly inflammatory fibroblasts in Smillie 2019), a lineage all four atlases agree on, and antibody-tractable; partly composition, with no response or functional data.

failed class as open.text: First in the convergence ranking and up in all eight cohorts, but neutrophils make almost all of its transcripts (neutrophil_share_inflamed = 0.965) and only a small change survives composition adjustment (adjusted_log2fc = 0.4409). As a target it was tested and not advanced: two antagonists, SB-656933 and navarixin, were approved in UC, and the antagonist navarixin (as MK-7123) lowered blood neutrophil counts dose-dependently in a COPD trial; a published genetic estimate, from one bioinformatic study, has higher expression going with lower UC risk, the direction opposite to an antagonist. As a biomarker it is higher at baseline in non-responders to ustekinumab and to placebo alike, which marks disease severity rather than response to the drug.
